executiveSummary: Analysis of 21 surveillance reports spanning October 2025 through May 2026 from ECDC and PAHO reveals multiple concurrent biological threats across Europe and the Americas. The most pressing concerns include ongoing Avian Influenza A(H5N1) activity with documented human spillover risk, elevated dengue and chikungunya transmission in the Americas, and resurging pertussis in the Western Hemisphere. Simultaneous circulation of seasonal influenza, RSV, and mpox adds compounding pressure on regional health systems, while yellow fever activity and measles outbreaks signal vaccination coverage gaps.
bottomLine: The Americas and Europe face a complex multi-pathogen threat environment in early-to-mid 2026, with Avian Influenza A(H5N1) and resurgent vector-borne diseases representing the highest-priority concerns requiring immediate coordinated response.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained regional activity
Documented animal reservoir activity with ongoing human spillover risk across the Americas
Dual PAHO alerts within 4-month window suggest escalating surveillance concern
threats.action: Enhance zoonotic surveillance at human-animal interfaces, activate pandemic preparedness protocols, and ensure antiviral stockpiles and H5N1 vaccine candidates are positioned for rapid deployment

threats.name: Dengue
signals: Epidemiological update issued February 2026 during Southern Hemisphere high-transmission season
Concurrent chikungunya alert suggests shared Aedes aegypti vector pressure and co-circulation risk
Historical hyperendemicity in Latin America and Caribbean amplifies outbreak potential
threats.action: Strengthen vector control operations, enhance dengue case surveillance and serotype monitoring, and prepare healthcare capacity for potential surge in hemorrhagic cases

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza
signals: PAHO alert issued 27 April 2026 marking start of Southern Hemisphere 2026 season
Prior alert in December 2025 for Northern Hemisphere 2025-26 season onset indicating year-round hemispheric burden
January 2026 alert for simultaneous RSV co-circulation creating compounded respiratory disease pressure
threats.action: Accelerate Southern Hemisphere influenza vaccination campaigns, monitor vaccine strain match, and prepare ICU and antiviral surge capacity for dual respiratory pathogen season

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two separate epidemiological updates issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained and escalating transmission
Dual alerts within 4-month period suggest failure to control initial resurgence wave
Resurgence pattern consistent with waning vaccine immunity and coverage gaps across the region
threats.action: Audit national immunization coverage rates, prioritize booster campaigns for adolescents and adults, and ensure maternal Tdap vaccination programs are functioning to protect neonates

threats.name: Mpox
signals: Dedicated epidemiological update issued 23 April 2026 indicating active regional transmission
Ongoing monitoring required given clade diversification observed globally in 2024-2025
Continued surveillance pressure from PAHO suggests cases remain above baseline thresholds
threats.action: Maintain JYNNEOS vaccination programs for high-risk populations, ensure diagnostic capacity at regional laboratories, and monitor for clade Ib importation events

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: Epidemiological alert issued March 2026 indicating active transmission or spillover events
Epizootic activity in non-human primates historically precedes human cases in the Americas
Unvaccinated travelers and populations in sylvatic transmission zones at heightened risk
threats.action: Strengthen yellow fever vaccination coverage in endemic and buffer zones, enhance epizootics surveillance in non-human primate populations, and issue travel health advisories for affected areas

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: Epidemiological alert issued February 2026 coinciding with high Aedes vector activity season
Concurrent dengue alert indicates shared ecological drivers and potential for simultaneous outbreak amplification
Prior Caribbean and Latin American epidemic history demonstrates rapid regional spread potential
threats.action: Integrate chikungunya surveillance with dengue vector control programs, enhance clinical training for differential diagnosis, and monitor for potential spread to naive populations

threats.name: Measles
signals: Epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating active cases or importation risk in a region that previously achieved elimination
Alert during February suggests potential linkage to global resurgence and post-COVID immunization gaps
Threat to regional elimination status representing a significant public health setback
threats.action: Conduct urgent vaccination coverage assessments, implement reactive vaccination campaigns in identified gaps, and strengthen measles surveillance and case-confirmation laboratory capacity

amrSignals: No explicit AMR-specific reports identified in the 21 surveillance documents; however, Bordetella pertussis macrolide resistance should be monitored given resurgence pattern documented in dual PAHO alerts
Dengue and arboviral co-circulation may mask bacterial co-infections requiring antibiotic treatment, increasing empiric antibiotic pressure and AMR selection risk in endemic regions
emergingPatterns: Dual hemispheric influenza burden creating year-round respiratory disease pressure with overlapping Northern and Southern Hemisphere seasons identified across December 2025 and April 2026 alerts
Vector-borne disease co-circulation (dengue + chikungunya) under shared Aedes aegypti pressure in the Americas signals ecological conditions favorable for simultaneous multi-pathogen outbreaks
Repeated pertussis resurgence alerts within a 4-month window suggest vaccine-derived immunity waning at population level, potentially indicating a broader immunization program erosion post-COVID
Avian influenza A(H5N1) persistence across the Americas with sustained PAHO monitoring from November 2025 through March 2026 indicates enzootic establishment rather than transient incursion

Measles re-emergence alert in a previously elimination-certified region reflects COVID-19 pandemic immunization debt and represents a canary-in-the-coalmine signal for broader vaccine-preventable disease resurgence
Concurrent ECDC weekly threat reports across five consecutive weeks (April-May 2026) suggest sustained elevated European communicable disease activity requiring ongoing multi-pathogen monitoring
